notes: The opening no is read as rule 35's fusion of kol with the clause's lo', discontinuous across the intervening relative clause; the competing reading would give no to kol and mark lo' unrepresented, which rule 35 forbids where one English word answers to two morphemes.

Both verbless possessive clauses put hath on the be- under rule 43; in the first the written relative supplies the English subject so the suffix is unrepresented, while in the second the suffix takes he.
made by fire is kept with 'ishshey as one discontinuous unit, headed on offerings by rule 31's tie-breaker, as at LEV.21.6.
